description:
kith-attach/src/lib.rs: the BlobStore public API lacks concurrency and idempotency contracts on several methods:

1. write_blob() and write_blob_streaming(): use a random nonce in the temp filename to handle concurrent writes for the same blob_id. This is correct, but the behavior on concurrent writes is not documented. Specifically: if two callers race to write the same blob_id, both will succeed and the final file will be whichever rename() wins (atomic on POSIX). This idempotent-last-write-wins behavior is a contract callers need to know about.

2. blob_path() (line 54): asserts validate_blob_id() is Ok. This is a public method that panics on invalid input without returning an error. The doc comment mentions the assert, but making a method pub when it can panic on user-supplied input is a defensive-code-forcing issue — every caller must call validate_blob_id() first or risk a panic. Since blob_path() just joins a path, it should either be pub(crate) (the path itself is an implementation detail) or return Result<PathBuf, String>.

3. init() returns io::Result<()> but write_blob() returns Err with NotFound if init() was not called. This init()-before-use contract is not type-enforced; the doc on write_blob() mentions it but init() itself does not document that it must be called before any write.

4. No concurrency documentation on the struct itself — BlobStore is Send + Sync (implicitly, since it only contains a PathBuf), and write_blob is &self not &mut self, meaning concurrent writes are possible. This is intentional (temp+rename is atomic) but not documented.
title: kith-attach: BlobStore methods undocumented for concurrency and idempotence
